body.v: To be refunded, this year's receipts must be uploaded by 31 December.
You can upload them in the HelvetiCare app, under Claims. It only takes a few minutes.
We never ask for receipts or bank details by email.

hotspots.explain: Sender's domain: helveticare.example, the insurer's own.
The deadline is real, and everything is spelled out: what to send, where, and by when. A deadline alone does not make an email a scam.
It sends you to the app, not to a link.
The insurer states that it never asks for receipts or bank details by email.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: HelvetiCare: the address is on helveticare.example.

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: A little urgency, from a real deadline, with no threat and no trick.
choices: Fear of a fine or a penalty
A little urgency, tied to a real deadline
None, it is just a newsletter

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Upload your receipts in the app. No receipts and no bank details by email.
choices: Upload the receipts in the app
Click a link and sign in

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Open the HelvetiCare app yourself, which is exactly what the email suggests.
choices: Look for a sign-in link in the email

actions.label: Open the HelvetiCare app yourself and upload the receipts
actions.consequence: The upload goes through, and your claim arrives on time.

actions.label: Make a note and upload the receipts next week
actions.consequence: No problem: the deadline is real, you just need to remember it.

actions.label: Reply with the receipts attached
actions.consequence: The insurer said so: it never asks for receipts by email. Use the app.

attacker_reveal: HelvetiCare really did send this one: a deadline, yes, but the right domain, no link, and everything handled in the app. Bin every email with a deadline and you will lose your refunds without me lifting a finger.
